correctness.rationale: The exact 19-tetrahedron source sphere minus the seven listed tetrahedra gives the published 12 facets and f=(8,25,30,12). An independently written face-closure/memoized recursion enumerated all non-evasive deletion and link cases and obtained roots 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7. A distinct pure shedding recursion returned root 5 only. For each other vertex the deletion maximal-face profile contains both triangles and tetrahedra, hence violates purity before recursion. For vertex5, the deletion is pure with nine tetrahedra and both deletion/link branches recursively vertex-decomposable, consistent with the source's explicit valid sequence starting 5,2,4,0,1. These are exhaustive finite decisions on the actual finite complex, not partial searches.

value.rationale: The minimal non-extendably-collapsible canonical ball is a natural stress test for recursive simplification. Demonstrating maximum first-step robustness under non-evasiveness versus unique first-step rigidity under pure vertex-decomposability is a meaningful complete local classification, not an arbitrary one-vertex check. It illustrates two notions that are often compared only through existence implications.

final_claim: For the canonical Benedetti--Lutz eight-vertex, twelve-tetrahedron non-extendably-collapsible ball, every one of the eight vertices is an admissible first vertex in the standard non-evasive recursion, whereas exactly the labelled vertex \(5\) is an admissible first pure vertex-decomposable shedding vertex; deleting each other vertex leaves a non-pure complex.
limitations: Only the first recursive step on the exact published labelled ball, not all future paths or all balls.
